content.title: The Circus Orchestra
content.story: The Circus Orchestra has quit. Every last one of them — tuba player, accordion, calliope operator — walked off the job this morning over a disagreement about peanuts. The show opens in 20 minutes and there is absolutely no music. The Ringmaster is panicking. Your patrol has been handed a pile of random objects and one impossible instruction: "Make it sound like a Circus." Every great Circus needs music. Every great Scout makes do with what they have. Figure it out. Make some noise. Make it glorious.
content.challenge: Using only improvised instruments made from provided materials, perform an original Circus-themed musical number for the judges. Score is based on creativity, performance quality, number of different improvised instruments used, and overall Circus spirit.
content.description: Your patrol is given access to a collection of provided objects that can be used as improvised instruments (buckets, cans, sticks, bottles, rubber bands, combs, etc.). The patrol has 5 minutes of preparation time to create instruments and organize their performance. They then perform for the judges for a minimum of 60 seconds. The performance must have a clear Circus feel — the judges are looking for rhythm, energy, creativity, and teamwork. All patrol members must participate in some musical role.
rules: All patrol members must participate — every Scout plays something
Only provided/improvised instruments may be used — no real instruments brought from camp
Scouts may use their voices (humming, beatboxing, sound effects)
The performance must have a recognizable Circus theme or feel
Judges score each patrol independently — no head-to-head comparison during scoring
content.time_and_scoring:
Points-based, 60 points + up to 10 bonus:
- Circus spirit and energy: 0–20 (subjective)
- Creativity and originality: 0–20 (subjective)
- Teamwork — all members contributing musically: 0–10
- Performance quality — rhythm, coordination, entertainment: 0–10
- Bonus: 1 point per distinct improvised instrument type incorporated (max 10 bonus points)
content.setup: Assemble collection of improvised instrument materials at station: buckets, tin cans, wooden sticks, empty bottles, rubber bands over boxes, combs + wax paper, shakers, washboard, spoons, etc. Stage materials in a visible pile. Mark a clear performance area. Brief judges on scoring criteria before event opens.
content.reset: Return all materials to the pile. Estimated reset time: 1–2 minutes.
content.staffing: 1–2 judges. Judges should be enthusiastic — this game feeds on energy. A stone-faced judge kills the performance. Consider recruiting a musically-inclined adult or OA member.
content.supplies_text:
5-gallon buckets (percussion): 2–3
Tin cans of various sizes: 6–8
Wooden dowels or sticks (striking): 6–8
Empty glass or plastic bottles (blowing): 4–6
Rubber bands (assorted sizes): 1 bag
Small cardboard boxes (rubber band guitar base): 2–3
Combs + wax paper (kazoo): 4–6 sets
Small containers with rice/pebbles sealed inside (shakers): 4–6
Metal spoons (rhythm): 4–6 pairs
Washboard (optional): 1
Any other interesting noise-making objects available on site
content.notes: The improvised instrument BONUS scoring is what rewards preparation and creativity — a patrol that assigns each member a different instrument and practices for the full 5 minutes will score more bonus points than one that all beats buckets together. Keep the preparation time strictly timed — 5 minutes, then perform. Position this station near the main gathering area if possible — it's entertaining for the whole camp.
